title: Longest Run of Identical Characters
statement:
Given a string `s`, find the length of the longest run of **identical consecutive characters**, that is, the longest substring in which every character is the same.

For example, in `aabbbcccdddd` the longest run is `dddd`, so the answer is `4`.

Think about the edge cases: the string may be empty (the answer is `0`), it may consist of a single repeated character, and the comparison is case-sensitive, so `a` and `A` are different characters.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `n`, the length of `s`.
If `n > 0`, the second line contains the string `s` (no spaces). If `n = 0` the string is empty and there is no second line.
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the length of the longest run of identical consecutive characters.
constraints: s consists of English letters (uppercase and lowercase) and digits

examples.explanation: The runs are aa, bbb, ccc and dddd; the longest has length 4.
The string is empty, so there is no run at all.
Matching is case-sensitive: the runs are A, a, AA and aaa, so the longest run is 3.

hints: Walk through the string once and keep the length of the run that ends at the current character.
If the current character equals the previous one, extend the run; otherwise restart it at 1.
Keep the maximum of all run lengths, and start it at 0 so the empty string works.
